rationale: Follow the registered question 486d1abb02d149b084c6a6800b992c97-question-1 with a direct probe of the message shapes that reach the read-index producer. The captured dispatch treats MsgReadIndex as a term-less message that followers forward unchanged (raft.go:1759-1765) and that a leader passes straight to sendMsgReadIndexResponse (raft.go:1346-1363, 2142-2157), while the only entry-count guard on this path belongs to MsgReadIndexResp (raft.go:1766-1772) and the only deliberate empty-payload guard belongs to MsgProp (raft.go:1286-1289). The harness therefore steps five real message shapes through the real Step entry points of a freshly elected three-voter cluster - empty and one-entry MsgReadIndex on the leader, empty MsgProp on the leader as the guarded contrast, and empty and one-entry MsgReadIndex on a follower to observe the forwarding hop - recovering any panic only in the harness and reporting the recovered value verbatim together with the node's state, term and read-index bookkeeping.

scope.description: In-process three-voter cluster (nodes 1, 2, 3 of the captured raft package, three real state machines per probe, a freshly elected leader per probe) with the default ReadOnlySafe option. Each probe feeds one message through the real Step entry point of the addressed node and records what the state machine did, including a panic recovered by the harness.
assumptions: MsgReadIndex and MsgProp shapes that a peer could deliver are represented by constructing the pb.Message directly and stepping it into the addressed node; the harness replicates what the captured library would receive from a transport.
The leader has committed an entry in its term before the probes, so the read-index producer is reached directly instead of appending to pendingReadIndexMessages.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no network, snapshot, membership or restart event is injected.
The panic is recovered only by the harness. In production the same panic escapes (*raft).Step and aborts the caller's raft loop, which is why the recovered value is reported verbatim.
excluded: The embedding application's transport and message validation, which is outside the captured package
Byzantine peers, admission control and message authentication
ReadOnlyLeaseBased, pendingReadIndexMessages, membership change and leader change
Any state-machine effect of a proposal, since the probes carry either no payload or one payload and are not applied

experiment.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). assuranceCluster builds three real raft instances with newTestRaft(1|2|3, 10, 1, newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), wires them with newNetwork and elects node 1 by nt.send(MsgHup); it asserts r1.state == StateLeader and r1.committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and then clears the message queues. For each probe the harness builds a fresh cluster, selects the target node (the leader for role 'leader', follower 2 for role 'follower'), emits a probe_setup event with the target's term and state, and constructs pb.Message{From: target.id, To: target.id, Type: MsgReadIndex or MsgProp, Entries: payload} where payload is empty or holds one entry. It emits a read_index_step (or prop_step) admission event carrying probe_id, role, entries, message type, node, term, log_committed and log_applied, then calls assuranceStepRecover, which steps the message and recovers any panic, and emits the outcome event with panicked, the verbatim recovered value, the number and types of emitted messages, and the target's state, term, pending/queue sizes and committed index after the step, followed by a probe_done event. Probes: 'leader/empty-entries' (MsgReadIndex, no Entries) is expected to panic, 'leader/one-entry' (MsgReadIndex, one entry) is the positive control expected to emit heartbeats and create one pending status, 'leader/empty-prop' (MsgProp, no Entries) is the guarded contrast expected to panic with the library's own message, 'follower/empty-entries' and 'follower/one-entry' are expected to forward exactly one MsgReadIndex to the leader. The test asserts these observed outcomes so that a behaviour change fails the test instead of reshaping the evidence.
experiment.responsibility: A node that processes a message delivered to it by a peer must not abort the process because of that message's shape: it must reject, drop or otherwise handle the shape. The captured library makes that choice explicitly for proposals (MsgProp with no entries panics deliberately) and validates the entry count for MsgReadIndexResp, so the same duty applies to the MsgReadIndex path that enters the leader's read-index producer.

comparisons.description: Stepping a MsgReadIndex with no Entries into a leader does not panic the node.
Control: stepping a well-formed MsgReadIndex with one entry into a leader does not panic the node.
Control: stepping the same read-index shapes into a follower does not panic the node.
Contrast: an empty MsgProp panics deliberately with the library's own guard message.
